title: Corn Kernel: Parts of the Corn Plant, Kinds, Uses and Price
metaTitle: Corn Kernel: Parts, Kinds, Uses and Price in the Philippines
metaDescription: What is a corn kernel? See the parts of the corn plant and ear, how each kernel forms, the kinds of mais, their uses and the June 2026 PSA corn prices.
keywords: corn seed grow a garden roblox
excerpt: A corn kernel is both the seed and the grain of the corn plant. Farmers plant it, feed mills buy it and families cook it as mais. This guide explains the parts of the corn plant and ear and how each kernel forms. It also covers the kinds grown in the Philippines, their uses from feeds to corn flakes, and the latest corn kernel price from the PSA.

blocks.text: What a corn kernel is

If you searched for corns in Tagalog, the word is mais, and a field planted to corn is a maisan. A single grain is a butil ng mais. Every corn kernel is a complete seed, so the grain you sell and the seed you plant are the same thing, only handled differently.

The corn scientific name is Zea mays L. Corn belongs to the grass family, Poaceae, the same family as [palay](/crops/palay) and sugarcane. That is also why a few pests, such as the fall armyworm, can feed on both corn and rice.

Inside, a corn kernel has three main parts. The hull, or pericarp, is the thin outer skin. Most of the grain is endosperm, the starch that feeds the young plant. Near the narrow end lies the germ, or embryo, which grows into the new seedling. That narrow end, the tip cap, is where the kernel joined the cob.
Parts of the corn plant and ear
A corn plant carries its male and female flowers in different places. Knowing each part helps you read the crop, because pests and stress show up on different parts at different stages.

blocks.caption: Parts of the corn plant and what each one does
rows: Seminal roots feed the seedling first. Permanent roots then grow from the lower nodes, and brace roots near the soil help hold the stalk up.
Moves water and food between roots, leaves and ear. The Asian corn borer tunnels inside it.
Make food for the plant. Losing leaves close to flowering hurts yield more than early leaf damage.
The male flower at the top. It sheds the pollen.
The female flower. It forms at a node on the stalk and becomes the ear you harvest.
Leafy layers that wrap the ear and shield the kernels from rain, birds and insects.
Long threads from the tip of the ear. Each silk leads to one ovule, a future kernel.
The core that holds the kernels in rows.
The grain and the seed. It fills with starch after fertilization.

blocks.text: Corn husk: more than a wrapper

In Tagalog the corn husk is balat ng mais, the silk is buhok ng mais and the cob is busal. The husk also tells you when to harvest. When the husk and some leaves turn from green to dry, and a black layer forms at the base of the kernels, the grain has reached maturity, according to the DA Cagayan Valley corn techno guide.

After harvest, husks still have uses. Cooks in Bukidnon and Bogo, Cebu wrap binaki, a steamed sweet corn cake, in corn husks. Dry husks also go to cattle and goats, into compost, or into handicrafts.
When fertilization occurs in corn

Corn flowers only once, and those few days decide how full each cob will be. Fertilization occurs when a grain of pollen from the tassel lands on a fresh silk. The pollen grows a tube down the silk to its ovule, and fertilization follows within about 24 hours, based on Iowa State University extension.

Every ovule on the ear has its own silk. So one silk that catches pollen gives one corn kernel, while a silk that misses leaves a gap on the cob. Silks stay receptive for about ten days, and a whole field sheds pollen over roughly 10 to 14 days.

Drought or poor nutrition at this stage delays silking more than pollen shed, so the ear ends up with poor seed set. That is why the DA guide names the reproductive stage as the time to give supplemental water. On anee.io, the [growth stages](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) view shows which lots are near tasseling and silking on any date you pick, along with the weather forecast for each lot.
Kinds of corn kernel in the Philippines
When farmers ask which corn breed to plant, they usually mean one of four kernel types. Each variety of corn fits a market, so pick the type first and the brand second.

blocks.caption: Corn kernel types grown in the Philippines and their usual markets
rows: Hard yellow kernels, mostly hybrid seed
Hog and poultry feeds, starch, oil
Hard white flint kernels, hybrid or OPV
Corn grits and mais rice, flour, snacks
White kernels that turn sticky when cooked
Boiled or roasted green corn, soups, sticky snacks

blocks.text: For help choosing a variety, see our guide to [corn seeds](/crops/corn-seeds). It covers hybrids, open pollinated varieties and the GM corn approved in the Philippines. For a planting guide in Filipino, read [pagtatanim ng mais](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).
What corn kernels become

items: **Feeds.** Yellow corn goes mainly into hog and poultry feeds, so feed mills and traders are its main buyers.

**Corn grits and [mais rice](/crops/mais-rice).** White corn milled into small grits and cooked like rice is a daily staple in parts of the Visayas and Mindanao, and in some towns of Isabela and Cagayan.
**Corn bran.** Milling strips off the hull and some of the germ. This corn bran goes into animal feeds, and food makers also use it as a source of fiber.
**Corn flakes.** Factories cook milled corn, roll it thin and toast it to make corn flakes.
**Starch, oil and syrup.** Processors also turn corn into starch, cooking oil, syrup and flour.

blocks.text: Gulay na mais: corn eaten as a vegetable

Gulay na mais, also said mais na gulay, means corn picked green and cooked as a vegetable. Glutinous and sweet corn fill this market. The DA Cagayan Valley guide notes that green glutinous corn, boiled or roasted, is a popular snack and also goes into soups and vegetable dishes.

At home that means nilagang mais, sinabawang mais with malunggay, and ginataang mais. For a bigger green ear, the same guide suggests a wider spacing of 30 by 75 centimeters.
Corn kernel price in the Philippines

Buyers quote corn per kilo of shelled grain, and the price moves with the season. Below are national farmgate averages from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) OpenSTAT table. blocks.text:
Your own corn kernel price can sit far from these averages. Buyers pay less for wet grain, broken kernels, dirt and moldy corn. The DA guide recommends drying grain to 14 percent moisture or lower for safe storage. It also gives aflatoxin limits of 20 ppb for food corn and 50 ppb for feeds. Distance to the buyer matters too, and prices often dip when every maisan in the area harvests at once.

On the paid plans of anee.io, the [farm reports](/features/farm-reports) keep each buyer, price and yield per season, so next year you can compare. For rice prices, see our [palay price guide](/blog/palay-price-philippines).

blocks.title: Check the cob before you sell
blocks.text: Pull back the husk on a few ears from different parts of the field. Gaps at the tip point to poor pollination or cut silks, while holes and frass point to borers. Write down what you see so you can plan next season.

blocks.text: Pests that damage the kernel

Watch for these pests from the whorl stage to harvest. The [asiatic corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer) bores into stalks, tassels and ear shanks, and in bad attacks the ears break and drop. The [fall armyworm](/pests/fall-armyworm) feeds in the whorl and can later bore into the ears. Corn earworms also cut the silks, which leaves unfilled kernels at the tip.
Corn kernel questions farmers ask

items.q: What is the corn scientific name?
items.a: Zea mays L. Corn belongs to the grass family, Poaceae, along with rice and sugarcane.
Corn is mais in Tagalog. A corn field is a maisan, a kernel is butil ng mais, the husk is balat ng mais and the silk is buhok ng mais.

items.q: Why does my corn cob have missing kernels?
items.a: Most gaps come from silks that never caught pollen. Drought, heat or poor nutrition near flowering can delay silking, and earworms can cut the silks. Borers feeding on the ear also leave damaged kernels.

items.q: Is yellow corn the same as white corn?
items.a: No. Yellow corn goes mostly to feeds, while white corn is the food corn milled into grits. Both are Zea mays, but they are different varieties.

items.q: Is this the corn seed from Grow a Garden?
items.a: No. The corn seed in the Roblox game Grow a Garden is only a game item. This page is about real corn kernels on Filipino farms, and our [corn seeds](/crops/corn-seeds) guide covers the seed you actually plant.
